references.text: Detailed instructions regarding the daily burnt offering with two one-year-old lambs, one in the morning and one in the evening, fulfilling the commandment in Exodus 29:38.
The introduction to the laws concerning the regular offerings that the Lord commanded Moses, including the daily offering.
A reference to the daily burnt offering maintained by the priests in temple service.
The restoration of the daily burnt offering after returning from exile, in accordance with the Mosaic Law.
The prophecy that the daily offering (tamid) will be removed, highlighting the significance of this practice.
The prophecy concerning the abolition of the daily offering, emphasizing its central role in temple service.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple includes the daily burnt offering of a one-year-old lamb each morning.
The daily offering performed by the priests is contrasted with Christ's single perfect sacrifice that takes away sins forever.
John the Baptist calls Jesus "the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world," fulfilling the symbolism of the daily lamb offering.
Christ is described as a lamb without blemish or defect, meeting the requirement for unblemished sacrificial lambs.
The legislative enactment of the same commandment regarding the continual burnt offering.
Specifies the times (morning and evening) for the two lambs mentioned in Exodus 29:38.
